title: A More Inclusive Workplace for Breastfeeding Mothers
what_it_is: A More Inclusive Workplace for Breastfeeding Mothers

sections.label: Exclusive breastfeeding rate increase
sections.summary: The rate of exclusive breastfeeding for at least six months rose from 1% in 2011 to a reported 38.2% in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For exclusive breastfeeding for at least six months, the rate has increased from 1% in 2011 to a reported 38.2% in 2019.

sections.label: Working mothers need lactation rooms
sections.summary: A local survey by the Breastfeeding Mothers Support Group Singapore found eight in 10 working mothers say a lactation room is among their greatest needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: According to the local survey by the Breastfeeding Mothers Support Group Singapore, eight in 10 working mothers say one of the things they need the most is a lactation room.

sections.label: Mandating lactation rooms in buildings
sections.summary: The Government must mandate more lactation rooms in office and business park buildings, as MND currently requires only one for buildings of 10,000 sqm or more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To really help breastfeeding mothers, the Government has to mandate the provision of more lactation rooms in buildings that have offices and business parks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Currently, MND requires only one lactation room for such buildings if they have a gross floor area of 10,000 square metres (sqm) or more.

sections.label: MND review of lactation room rules
sections.summary: It asks whether MND will lower the gross floor area threshold and increase the number of lactation rooms required in larger office and business park buildings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In its next review of the Code on Accessibility in the Built Environment, will MND consider lowering the gross floor area threshold, so that more buildings with offices and business parks will be required to have a lactation room?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will MND also consider increasing the number of lactation rooms required for larger buildings containing offices and business parks?

sections.label: Paid breastfeeding breaks laws
sections.summary: A 2020 report on 97 countries found that 73% of the countries had laws for paid breastfeeding breaks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A 2020 report on 97 countries found that 73% of the countries had laws for paid breastfeeding breaks.

sections.label: Legislating paid breastfeeding breaks
sections.summary: It asks whether the Government will consider legislation to mandate the provision of paid breaks specifically for breastfeeding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To support mothers at their workplaces, will the Government consider introducing legislation to mandate the provision of paid breaks, specifically, for breastfeeding?

sections.label: Breastfeeding rules across ministries
sections.summary: MHA, MOT and MOE clarify that breastfeeding in public is allowed and commit to lactation rooms in transport hubs, stations and schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: MHA has clarified that breastfeeding in public is unlikely to constitute offenses of indecent exposure or appearing nude in public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: MOT has made clear that breastfeeding is allowed on buses and trains and that the Government will provide nursing rooms at all new bus interchanges and integrated transport hubs, as well as new MRT interchange stations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: MOE has said that it is committed to providing a conducive workplace for nursing mothers and will ensure that all Primary schools, Secondary schools and Junior Colleges/centralised institutes have a dedicated lactation room.

sections.label: Paid lactation breaks legislation
sections.summary: The passage states the need to join most countries and introduce legislation providing paid lactation breaks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Second, we need to join the majority of countries and introduce legislation to provide paid lactation breaks.

sections.label: BCA lactation room requirements
sections.summary: BCA required family-friendly features like lactation rooms in new and retrofitted buildings in 2014, extending this to more building types in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In 2014, BCA introduced requirements for new buildings and existing buildings undergoing major retrofits to provide family-friendly features,such as lactation rooms.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In 2020, BCA extended the requirement to more building types, including offices and business parks exceeding 10,000 sqm in GFA.

sections.label: BCA Accessibility Fund retrofits
sections.summary: Building owners can tap BCA's Accessibility Fund, which co-funds up to 60% of construction costs, extended on 1 August to buildings built between 1990 and 2014.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Building owners who wish to retrofit their buildings with family-friendly features, such as lactation rooms, can tap on BCA's Accessibility Fund (AF), which co-funds up to 60% of the construction cost of such features.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To support more of such progressive building owners, BCA extended the AF on 1 August to all buildings built between 1990 and 2014, when the requirements for family-friendly features were first introduced.

sections.label: Employers supporting nursing mothers
sections.summary: Infineon provides lactation rooms and flexible work arrangements, and tripartite partners promote best practices, NTUC's campaign and the Made For Families initiative.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: For example, Infineon Technologies supports nursing mothers at work by providing private lactation rooms and flexible work arrangements (FWAs), such as hybrid work and flexi-hours.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Together with our tripartite partners, we are supporting employers to do more for nursing mothers at work.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We will continue to promote best practices with the Employer's Guide to Breastfeeding at the Workplace.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: NTUC also supports companies to adopt family-friendly practices under their "Better Workplace" campaign, which includes the provision of nursing facilities.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: These companies can also participate in the Made For Families initiative to be recognised as supportive employers.

sections.label: Clarification on next year's review
sections.summary: The passage records a question to Mr Louis Ng and a mention that a review will take place next year.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: Mr Louis Ng, are you seeking a clarification?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: I think she mentioned that there will be a review next year.

sections.label: Breastfeeding rate and review timing
sections.summary: About a third of mothers still breastfeed at six months, and a review of marriage and parenthood support is being asked to be expedited to this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: The data that I shared showed that about a third of mothers are still breastfeeding when the infant is six months old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Data shows that there is a lack of it now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: I am wondering again when the review will be completed and whether we could expedite and do it this year, instead of next year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We are reviewing a whole range of things in support of marriage and parenthood.
